items.summary: Disha Salian died in June 2020. A young talent manager working in Bollywood, she tragically fell to her death from the 12th storey of a flat in Mumbai on the intervening night of June 8 and 9, 2020. But the claims surrounding the death of the 28-year-old refuse to die. This time, there is a new twist in this already convoluted sequence of events. Satish Salian spent five years after the sudden death of his daughter, Disha, trying his best to quash these rumours. He and his wife, Vasanti, would tell anyone who would listen – family members, friends, neighbours and journalists – that these claims were simply not true. items.title: Independent judge does not mean a judge who always goes against the executive and legislature: SG Tushar Mehta
items.summary: An independent judge does not necessarily mean one who constantly confronts the executive and legislature, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said on Thursday. Courts should not substitute their own policy preferences for policy decisions taken by elected governments, he emphasised. " Independent judge does not mean that a judge who always fights or remains in confrontation with the executive or legislature. Executive is not a political party. Executive is a constitutional organ which represents each and every citizen and is answerable to each and every citizen ," Mehta said. He emphasised that India has an independent judiciary. Mehta was speaking at a discussion on Shaping the Legal Architecture of Viksit Bharat 2047. The discussion, moderated by Sanjeev Gemawat ( Managing Director and Group General Counsel of Essar Group) was organised by the University of Chicago Center in Delhi, the Nani Palkhivala Foundation and the General Counsels' Association of India (GCAI). It also featured Delhi High Court Justice Prathiba M Singh , Senior Advocate Arvind Datar and Atal Innovation Mission Director Deepak Bagla . Mehta said elected governments have the mandate to formulate economic, financial and technological policies. Courts could examine their constitutionality but could not assume the executive's role and reframe policies. "What I always call, and I'm criticised for calling it, 'NGO activism' is not permissible in judiciary. They cannot replace and reframe a policy unless it can be shown there is a violation of fundamental rights, " he said. Mehta also criticised certain past environmental judgments, claiming that they had set India’s economic development back by nearly two decades. " Even if they bonafide believe in a particular policy, can they make it applicable to 140 crore Indians who have voted the other organ to do that? " he asked. The Solicitor General clarified that his observations were personal and not made on behalf of the government. He distinguished judicial intervention from judicial innovation. He said that courts must intervene against unconstitutional executive or legislative action but could not formulate alternative policies. " Innovation is not something which is given to judiciary. items.title: Authorities can't pass orders blindly based on panel lawyer's legal opinion: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that administrative and statutory authorities cannot pass executive orders blindly, relying solely the legal opinion of their panel advocates. Justice T M Nadaf held that legal opinions given by panel advocates are only advisory in nature and cannot replace the independent decision-making process of the competent authority. The Court added that an authority that merely copies or approves a legal opinion without examining the relevant facts and law abdicates its statutory power and acts under dictation. “ If an authority blindly copies or signs off the order only on the legal opinion, without examining the facts and relevant law by itself, it amounts to an abdication of statutory power and acting under dictation. Such orders require to be held as arbitrary, invalid and lacking jurisdiction ,” the Court said. . The Court passed the order on a petition filed by a woman named Sangamma, who challenged an endorsement issued by the Executive Officer of the Kushtagi Taluk Panchayat on June 6, 2023. The endorsement had been issued after an earlier High Court direction to consider her representation. The petitioner had also filed a contempt of court petition against the local authority for not examining her representation despite a court directive. These contempt proceedings were dropped after the officer claimed that he had complied with the Court's order. The petitioner, however, was granted liberty to challenge the endorsement issued by the officer on her representation. The Court found that the officer had failed to independently apply his mind to the petitioner's grievance in accordance with the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj Act, 1993. “It appears, the order came to be passed in a haste, only to absolve themselves from the contempt proceedings and to save their skin. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes case against man booked for morphed image of Rahul Gandhi with Pakistani army officer
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against a man booked for sharing a Facebook post with an edited image that depicted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alongside a Pakistani Army officer with a tagline “one agenda.” Justice M Nagaprasanna passed the order on a petition filed by the accused, one G Nagesh alias Rajesha Hir imane. “If the facts obtaining in the case at hand are considered on the bedrock of the principles laid down by the Apex Court, permitting further trial in the case at hand would become an abuse of the process of law and result in miscarriage of justice,” the Court's November 4 order said. Justice M Nagaprasanna and Karnataka High Court Nagesh (petitioner) had been booked under Section 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for allegedly promoting enmity, hatred and ill-will between communities and regional groups through the post. items.summary: The Kerala High Court has held that transport authorities cannot refuse to process applications relating to vehicle registration, merely because traffic challans issued before October 1, 2020, remain unpaid. [TN Kumar v Ministry of Road Transport and Highways & ors] Justice Murali Purushothaman held that Rule 167(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (Rules) as amended , which restricts certain vehicle-related services when traffic challans remain unpaid, cannot be applied to violations that occurred before the provision came into force. The Court explained that the rule introduced a restriction that did not previously exist and could therefore operate only from the date it came into force. It clarified that unless the law clearly provided otherwise, a new restriction could not be imposed on the basis of challans issued before the rule was introduced. " Rule 167(7) being substantive law, operates prospectively as retrospectivity is not clearly made out by its language. Therefore, in the absence of a clear legislative intention to confer retrospective effect on Rule 167(7), the provision cannot be invoked to interdict the processing of applications for registration of motor vehicles merely on the ground that challans issued prior to 01.10.2020 remain pending against the applicants, " the Court added. Justice Murali Purushothaman The judgment came on a petition filed by TN Arun Kumar, who had purchased a car in 2015 through a loan from Bank of Baroda. After repaying the loan, Kumar approached the Regional Transport Office at Ernakulam to remove the bank's hypothecation entry from the vehicle's registration certificate. However, he was informed that his vehicle had been blacklisted because certain traffic challans were unpaid for more than 90 days. Aggrieved, Kumar approached the Court, submitting that he had already paid the fines relating to challans issued after October 1, 2020, while the unpaid challans were related to speeding violations between 2015 and 2019, before Rule 167(7) of the Rules came into force. The Court examined Rule 167, which was introduced through the Central Motor Vehicles (Eleventh Amendment) Rules, 2020 and came into force on October 1, 2020. items.title: Old Monk withdraws plea in Bombay High Court against FSSAI ban
items.summary: The manufacturer of iconic rum brand Old Monk on Thursday withdrew its petition before the Bombay High Court challenging a prohibition order issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) that halted the sale of the beverage [ M/S. Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries Private Limited vs Union of India & Ors. ]. The FSSAI had halted Old Monk sales on grounds that it did not comply with proper labeling requirements. The FSSAI said that since the beverage used added flavouring, it must be labelled as a "rum-flavoured spirit." Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries Ltd, which manufactures and bottles Old Monk in Maharashtra, today told the High Court that it would submit revised product labels directly to the food safety regulator for approval. A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna proceeded to allow the Old Monk manufacturer to withdraw its plea challenging the FSSAI's prohibition order. Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna The dispute stemmed from a prohibition order passed by the FSSAI's Western Regional Office under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, halting the sale and distribution of Old Monk variants produced at the company’s Khopoli facility. The statutory regulator objected to the marketing and packaging of the beverage, asserting that it could not be sold merely under the generic classification of "rum." According to the FSSAI, the product was formulated predominantly using neutral alcohol and added nature-identical or artificial flavourings, meaning it must legally be declared on the packaging as a "rum-flavoured spirit" under the Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulations. The authority also took exception to age-related descriptors such as "7 Years Old Blended" and "Very Old Vatted." The manufacturer also later agreed to modify bottle labels after the High Court questioned the accuracy of its ageing claims during a hearing in August. The manufacturer had initially approached the High Court seeking to quash the ban, arguing that its formulations comply with applicable excise norms, are widely sold across other states. It also told the Court that the regulatory freeze on its sales had cost Maharashtra over ₹350 crore in excise revenue , apart from leaving hundreds of factory workers idle. items.title: With control of Congress, here’s how Democrats could stop Trump’s war in Iran
items.summary: The Democrats’ sweeping victory in the US midterm elections puts them in a stronger position to interfere with President Donald Trump’s agenda. This includes his deeply unpopular and costly war against Iran, which could be among their first priorities. As president, Trump will be able to veto any legislation aimed at ending the war. But the Democrats still have another powerful card up their sleeves: cutting off funding for the war. There are caveats, however. History suggests exercising this power could trigger a political confrontation that may backfire. And even if the Democrats succeed in ending the war, they may not be able to reverse the damage it has done to the US’ global standing. The limits of legislation Democrats will have three main options to try to force the war against Iran to a close. Two of these, however, face significant limitations. The first – and perhaps most obvious – option is through legislation. There are a few different ways to do this. One approach is to pass a resolution calling for an end to the war. Congress already attempted this in June, passing a concurrent resolution (with the support of some Republicans) that directed the president to either withdraw US forces from hostilities against Iran or seek the approval of Congress before continuing. This was done under the War Powers Resolution of 1973 . These so-called concurrent resolutions are, however, widely seen as non-binding . Intended to express the opinion or will of Congress, they are generally used to deal with internal matters within Congress. Trump ignored it. A similar resolution then failed in the Senate in September. For such a resolution to be binding, it would need the force of a law passed by Congress, which the president would likely veto. To overcome that veto, the Democrats would need the support of a two-thirds majority in both the House and the Senate. This would require a significant number of Republicans to cross the aisle. The Iran war is deeply unpopular with American voters. Exercising oversight A second option for the Democrats is to launch a series of congressional investigations into the way the war has been conducted. This would likely include public hearings, subpoenas and demands for documents from the Trump administration. The Democrats may also attempt to impeach senior officials in the Trump administration. items.title: Cyclone Murasu: 8 dead, CM Naidu estimates damages at Rs 1919 cr in Andhra
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the aftermath of Cyclone Murasu on Thursday, November 5, inquiring with officials about damage caused across various departments, including Agriculture, Electricity, Municipal Administration and Panchayat Raj. Officials reported that a total of eight people had died due to the cyclone—five in Bapatla district, two in Guntur district and one in Palnadu district. According to a preliminary damage assessment, Cyclone Murasu has caused an estimated loss of Rs 1,918.55 crore to the state. Agricultural crops were damaged across 1,43,122 hectares, affecting 1,86,063 farmers. Horticultural crops suffered damage across 6,749 hectares, impacting 12,586 farmers. A total of 983 houses, 346 boats and 220 fishing nets were also damaged, officials told the CM. They said it would take another 48–72 hours to assess the extent of crop damage accurately after floodwaters receded. A week before Murasu, at least seven people were killed when Cyclone Arnab lashed the state, and a preliminary estimate of losses stood at Rs 4,600 crore. With two consecutive cyclones affecting the state, the Chief Minister directed officials to ensure that farmers and the public do not face any hardships. He stressed the need to prioritise the restoration of electricity supply, repair of roads and uninterrupted drinking water supply. The Roads and Buildings (R&B) Department reported damage to 760 kilometres of major district roads and state highways. Under the Panchayat Raj Engineering Department, 74 rural roads were damaged, resulting in losses across 204 kilometres. The estimated cost of restoring these roads is Rs 92.08 crore, officials said. The Panchayat Raj Department reported that 59 mandals and 649 gram panchayats were affected by Cyclone Murasu. A total of 11 SDRF teams, 13 NDRF teams and 390 fire personnel participated in cyclone relief and rescue operations. Restoration of damaged electricity infrastructure, roads, drinking water systems and other essential infrastructure is underway.

items.title: SC declines plea to shift Tirumala ghee adulteration case from Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Supreme Court on Thursday, November 5, rejected a plea seeking the transfer of the trial in the Tirumala laddu ghee adulteration case from Andhra Pradesh, observing that the investigation was being handled by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Appearing for Maharashtra-based dairy businessman Machindra Shantaram Lanke, one of the accused, senior advocate Siddharth Dave argued that the political atmosphere in Andhra Pradesh was not conducive to a fair trial. He pointed to public statements made by Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, alleging that their remarks could prejudice the proceedings. Justice Joymalya Bagchi noted that the CBI was conducting the investigation and would not be influenced by comments from political leaders. Chief Justice Surya Kant said the court had already addressed such concerns and that the accused could approach it again if any interference occurred. The case concerns the alleged supply of adulterated ghee to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) between 2019 and 2024. Investigations by the CBI and Enforcement Directorate (ED) have uncovered an alleged large-scale fraud involving supplies valued at hundreds of crores. The controversy erupted in September 2024 when Chandrababu Naidu claimed that animal fat had been used in ghee supplied for preparing Tirumala laddus. The Supreme Court subsequently criticised the public statements, cautioning against bringing religious matters into political disputes. A chargesheet filed by the CBI-led Special Investigation Team in January 2026 found no evidence of animal fat in significant quantities. Instead, investigators alleged that synthetic ghee had been produced using palm oil, palm stearin and palm kernel oil. The ED's September 2026 investigation alleged that manufacturers also used chemical additives to imitate cow ghee, passing off the product as Agmark Special Grade cow ghee. The agency estimated the fraudulent supplies at around ₹230 crore and alleged that multiple dairy companies were involved in manufacturing, procurement and distribution. It has also accused the firms of maintaining fabricated purchase and sales records to disguise the transactions as legitimate ghee supplies. items.title: Bengaluru: Traffic curbs on Ballari Road for 18 months as BDA begins corridor work
items.summary: Commuters travelling on Ballari Road will face traffic restrictions for the next 18 months as the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) begins construction of an elevated corridor on Friday, November 6. The restrictions will affect commuters travelling between Hebbal, central Bengaluru and Kempegowda International Airport (KIA). The Bengaluru Traffic Police have prohibited all goods vehicles, including light, medium and heavy goods vehicles, as well as KSRTC and private buses, from using the affected stretch. Cars, two-wheelers and school buses can continue to use the road. The four-lane elevated corridor will run between the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS) staff quarters and Mehkri Circle, covering around 1.6 km. The stretch falls under the jurisdiction of the Sadashivanagar and Sanjaynagar traffic police stations. The construction is expected to take 18 months. The corridor is part of the BDA’s Rs 2,215-crore project to ease congestion at the Hebbal junction. The larger project includes a six-lane, cut-and-cover short tunnel between Hebbal junction and the Veterinary College, followed by an elevated corridor leading to Mehkri Circle, where a rotary flyover is planned. The project has also faced opposition, with the National Green Tribunal staying tree-felling until it decides on petitions challenging the work. The traffic police have advised motorists, including those travelling in emergency vehicles, to use alternative routes during the construction period. Vehicles travelling from central Bengaluru towards KIA via Hebbal should take the route through Old High Grounds Junction, Kalpana Junction, Old Udaya TV Junction, Cantonment Railway Station, Tannery Road and Nagawara Road before proceeding towards the airport. Those travelling from Yeshwantpur towards KIA should take Mathikere Road, turn right at BEL Circle and continue via Ring Road towards the airport. For vehicles travelling from KIA towards central Bengaluru, one option is to take a left turn at Hebbal, proceed towards Nagawara Junction, take a right turn and continue via Bamboo Bazaar and Queens Road. Alternatively, motorists can take a right turn at Hebbal and proceed via Hebbal Ring Road, Kuvempu Circle and Goraguntepalya Junction. They should then take a left turn and continue along Dr Rajkumar Road towards the city. Vehicles travelling from Yeshwantpur towards central Bengaluru should proceed via BHEL Junction, take a right turn near Maramma Circle and continue along Margosa Road.
